strings.name: Kevin Durant
strings.role: Basketball player · NBA and Olympic champion
strings.summary: After one season at Texas, Durant entered the NBA and became a prolific scorer by combining a forward’s height with shooting and ball handling. He won the 2014 regular-season MVP with Oklahoma City, then two titles and two Finals MVPs with Golden State. He later played for Brooklyn, Phoenix and Houston and returned from an Achilles injury. In Paris 2024 he became the first four-time men’s Olympic basketball gold medalist.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026. Selected career milestones; results and records refer to their cited dates, not an exhaustive results log or live ranking.
strings.influence.rationale: An NBA and Olympic champion whose scoring skills and international performances have had broad influence.

strings.facts.fact-2.label: College
strings.facts.fact-2.value: University of Texas at Austin; 2006–07 season
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Two titles and Finals MVPs
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Won championships and Finals MVP awards with Golden State in both 2017 and 2018.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Four Olympic basketball golds
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Won four gold medals with the United States from 2012 to 2024, a first in men’s Olympic basketball.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: All-NBA Second Team selection
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Earned All-NBA Second Team honors in his first season with Houston.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Traded to the Houston Rockets
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Moved from Phoenix to Houston in a seven-team trade.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Fourth Olympic gold
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Helped the United States beat France in Paris, becoming the first men’s player with four Olympic basketball golds.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Traded to Phoenix
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Moved from Brooklyn to Phoenix and joined Devin Booker in a new Western Conference setting.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Joined the Brooklyn Nets
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Joined Brooklyn in a sign-and-trade and missed a season with an Achilles injury before returning.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Second title and Finals MVP
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Helped Golden State repeat as champion and won a second consecutive Finals MVP.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: First NBA championship
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Won his first championship and Finals MVP against Cleveland in his first Golden State season.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Moved from Oklahoma City to Golden State
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Left Oklahoma City for Golden State, beginning the championship phase of his career.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: NBA regular-season MVP
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Won his first regular-season MVP with Oklahoma City and his fourth scoring title.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: College awards and NBA draft
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Became the first freshman Naismith college player of the year, then was drafted second by Seattle.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in Washington
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Born in Washington, DC, and developed in the region’s youth basketball system before attending Texas.
